items.statement: Manufacture all drugs in conformance with current good manufacturing practice.
items.quote: Section 501(a)(2)(B) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act requires all drugs to be manufactured in conformance with CGMP.

items.statement: Design manufacturing facilities and processes to prevent microbial contamination.
items.quote: Design manufacturing facilities(§ 211.42) and processes (see below) to prevent microbial contamination:

items.statement: For nonsterile drug products, establish control procedures to monitor output and validate processes, including bioburden testing.
items.quote: For nonsterile drug products, establish control procedures to monitor output and validate processes to include bioburden testing

items.statement: For nonsterile drug products, establish and follow written procedures designed to prevent the introduction of objectionable microorganisms.
items.quote: establish and follow written procedures designed to prevent the introduction of objectionable microorganisms

items.statement: For sterile drug products, establish and follow written procedures designed to prevent microbial contamination.
items.quote: For sterile drug products, establish and follow written procedures designed to prevent microbial contamination

items.statement: Conduct process validation studies to ensure acceptable output (for topical antiseptics, for example, particularly the microbiological quality of the product).
items.quote: Conduct process validation studies to ensure acceptable output (e.g., with topical antiseptics, particularly product microbiological quality)

items.statement: When deficient manufacturing steps, equipment or raw materials may be adversely affecting process control, implement and validate the needed changes.
items.quote: Implement and validate needed changes when deficient manufacturing steps, equipment, or raw materials may be adversely affecting process control.
items.condition: when deficient steps, equipment or raw materials may affect process control

items.statement: Ensure operating procedures will consistently produce a quality product.
items.quote: Ensure that operating procedures will consistently produce a quality product

items.statement: Review and evaluate any deviations or discrepancies documented during manufacturing and testing to determine whether a product lacks assurance of sterility (for sterile antiseptics) or may be contaminated with objectionable microorganisms (for nonsterile antiseptics).
items.quote: Review and evaluate any deviations or discrepancies documented during manufacturing and testing to determine if a product lacks assurance of sterility (for sterile antiseptics) or may be contaminated with objectionable microorganisms (for nonsterile antiseptics).

items.statement: Document and implement any corrective actions arising from the evaluation of deviations or discrepancies.
items.quote: Document and implement any corrective actions deriving from the evaluation

items.statement: Ensure all equipment, including water systems, operates consistently and is clean, sanitary and suitable for its intended use.
items.quote: Ensure that all equipment, including water systems, operates consistently and is clean, sanitary, and suitable for its intended use

items.statement: Establish and follow in-process bioburden testing procedures to help monitor in-process control, including understanding the bioburden challenge to a final sterilization process.
items.quote: Establish and follow in-process bioburden testing procedures to help monitor in-process control, including understanding the bioburden challenge to a final sterilization process

items.statement: Establish appropriate written testing standards or specifications and sampling plans for components, in-process materials, containers or closures, and finished products.
items.quote: Establish appropriate written testing standards/specifications and sampling plans for components, in-process materials, containers or closures, and finished products

items.statement: Establish procedures for testing and approving or rejecting components, drug product containers and closures.
items.quote: Establish procedures for testing and approval or rejection of components, drug product containers, and closures

items.statement: Test each lot of drug product component and of container or closure, including those that may be vulnerable to microbiological contamination, including applicator material (for example cotton pads) and water used as an ingredient in the product.
items.quote: Test each lot of a drug product component and container or closure, including those that may be vulnerable to microbiological contamination (§211.84)(d)(4-5), including applicator material (e.g., cotton pads) and water used as an ingredient in the product.

items.statement: Conduct appropriate microbiological tests before a batch disposition decision is made.
items.quote: Conduct appropriate microbiological tests before a batch disposition decision is made.

items.statement: Test each batch of a sterile product for sterility.
items.quote: Test each batch of a sterile product for sterility

items.statement: Test each batch of a non-sterile product to ensure the absence of objectionable microorganisms.
items.quote: Test each batch of a non-sterile product to ensure absence of objectionable microorganisms

items.statement: Management of the manufacturing facility must maintain a well-functioning quality system that includes an effective quality unit vested with the responsibilities and authorities CGMP requires.
items.quote: The CGMP regulations require that the management of a manufacturing facility maintains a well-functioning quality system, which includes an effective quality unit vested with the responsibilities and authorities required under CGMP

not_applicable.text: What specific CGMP regulations might be useful to manufacturers of topical antiseptic drug products?
The CGMP regulations in 21 CFR parts 210 and 211 for finished pharmaceuticals apply
The CGMP regulations provide the minimum legal requirements for conducting reliable operations
Some relevant CGMP regulations, with a brief description, are given below:
Manufacturing Design and Control: CGMP Requirements and Recommended Guidance for Manufacturers
See the guidance for industry Sterile Drug Products Produced by Aseptic Processing—Current Good Manufacturing Practice.

Components, In-Process Materials, Containers or Closures, and Finished Product Testing: CGMP Requirements for Manufacturers

items.statement: Perform a manufacturing risk assessment to understand manufacturing failure modes for microbial contamination and implement prevention measures.
items.quote: Because there are potentially many different root causes of product contamination by microorganisms, it is imperative that manufacturers perform a manufacturing risk assessment to understand manufacturing failure modes and implement prevention measures.

items.statement: Base the microbial contamination risk assessment on an understanding of the contamination vulnerabilities of the product concerned.
items.quote: In addition, any risk assessment approach should be informed by an understanding of the microbial contamination vulnerabilities of the concerned product.

items.statement: As part of the microbial contamination risk assessment, determine the types of microbes that might survive or thrive in the products.
items.quote: Determine the types of microbes that might survive or thrive in your products.

items.statement: Provide additional controls and testing based on the output of the microbial contamination risk assessment to ensure product quality.
items.quote: Provide additional controls and testing based on the output of the risk assessment to ensure product quality.

items.statement: Ensure microbial recovery methods can detect the types of microbes that may affect product quality.
items.quote: Ensure that your microbial recovery methods are capable of detecting the types of microbes that may affect product quality.

items.statement: As part of the microbial contamination risk assessment, evaluate the risk of contamination from components, including during component production and storage, and from the intrinsic risk of the source materials.
items.quote: Evaluate risk of contamination from components, including during component production, storage, or due to the intrinsic risk from source materials.

items.statement: Consider all possible sources of microbial contamination in the risk assessment.
items.quote: Consider all possible sources of microbial contamination, including the following:

items.statement: When considering sources of microbial contamination, consider that components or products stored in open bins can be contaminated by spore-forming microbes (such as Bacillus cereus), by Serratia species and by other airborne microbes.
items.quote: Components or products stored in open bins can be at risk for contamination by spore-forming microbes, such as Bacillus cereus, as well as by Serratia species and other worrisome airborne microbes

items.statement: When considering sources of microbial contamination, consider that manufacturing areas exposed to windy or poor HVAC conditions may increase this environmental contamination risk.
items.quote: Manufacturing areas exposed to windy or poor HVAC conditions may increase the potential for this environmental contamination risk.

items.statement: When considering sources of microbial contamination, consider that some materials, especially from natural sources, may have high or objectionable intrinsic bioburden.
items.quote: Some materials, especially from natural sources, may have high or objectionable intrinsic bioburden.

items.statement: When considering sources of microbial contamination, consider water quality as a significant risk where water is a key ingredient, as in most antiseptics.
items.quote: Water quality can pose a significant risk, as most antiseptics include water as a key ingredient.

items.statement: When considering sources of microbial contamination, consider unsanitary practices or sources.
items.quote: Unsanitary practices or sources.

items.statement: When considering sources of microbial contamination in areas with high humidity, give special attention to molds.
items.quote: When manufacturing in areas with high humidity, molds can be of special concern.

items.statement: Use sound risk management and stay aware of unusual microbiota reported in the literature that may affect the manufacturing processes (for example cell culture biotechnology or conventional sterile drug manufacturing).
items.quote: As a general principle, manufacturers should use sound risk management and be aware of unusual microbiota reported in the literature that may impact their manufacturing processes (e.g., cell culture biotechnology, conventional sterile drug manufacturing).

items.statement: Assess operations, be aware of potential risks and apply appropriate risk management based on an understanding of possible or emerging contamination risks.
items.quote: Manufacturers should assess their operations, be aware of potential risks, and apply appropriate risk management based on an understanding of possible or emerging contamination risks

items.statement: Implement preventive measures against contamination, as appropriate, during the product and process lifecycle.
items.quote: As appropriate, preventive measures should be implemented during the product and process lifecycle.

items.statement: If leptospiral contamination is considered possible or has occurred, include in risk mitigation a review of available published scientific literature and technical reports from related industry organizations that may help mitigate this hazard.
items.quote: Review of available published articles from the scientific literature and technical reports by related industry organizations that may provide further understanding on how to mitigate this contamination hazard.
items.condition: if leptospiral contamination is considered possible or has occurred

items.statement: If leptospiral contamination is considered possible or has occurred, include in risk mitigation the use, at appropriate intervals, of molecular or nonconventional microbial monitoring methods to detect microbial flora in processing steps or the immediate environment that current routine methods do not readily detect.
items.quote: Use of molecular or nonconventional microbial monitoring methods at appropriate intervals to detect microbial flora that may exist in processing steps or in the immediate environment, but are not readily detected by current routine methods.
items.condition: if leptospiral contamination is considered possible or has occurred

items.statement: Use the results of such expanded testing to modify the detection and control strategy (for example timing, frequency, types of tests) when a new risk is identified from a viable but not easily cultured microorganism.
items.quote: Such expanded testing should be used to modify the strategy (e.g., timing, frequency, types of tests) of detection and control in the event of newly identified risk posed by the viable, but not easily cultured, microorganism.
items.condition: newly identified risk from viable but not easily cultured microorganism

items.statement: Monitoring for Leptospira may use specialized media such as EMJH medium or other suitable media.
items.quote: Use of specialized media such as Ellinghausen McCullough Johnson Harris (EMJH) medium (Ellinghausen and McCullough 1965) or other suitable media (Rule and Alexander 1986).
items.condition: if leptospiral contamination is considered possible or has occurred

items.statement: Monitoring for spirochete bacteria may use validated polymerase chain reaction (PCR) methods for rapid screening and detection, for example as an investigative tool.
items.quote: Use of validated polymerase chain reaction (PCR) methods (e.g., as an investigative tool) for rapid screening and detection of spirochete bacteria.
items.condition: if leptospiral contamination is considered possible or has occurred

items.statement: Special stain techniques or other means may be considered to identify the presence of Leptospira.
items.quote: Consideration of special stain techniques or other means to identify the presence of Leptospira
items.condition: if leptospiral contamination is considered possible or has occurred

items.statement: Continue to properly use basic, standard microbiology laboratory practices to detect contamination.
items.quote: Firms should continue to properly employ basic, standard microbiology laboratory practices to detect contamination.

items.statement: Make microscopic examination part of the routine cell culture process control program in the laboratory.
items.quote: For example, the laboratory should ensure that microscopic examination is part of its routine cell culture process control program

items.statement: If leptospiral contamination is considered possible or has occurred, build quality risk-management measures into the initial design as preventive actions.
items.quote: Implementing such quality risk-management measures into the initial design (i.e., preventive actions)
items.condition: if leptospiral contamination is considered possible or has occurred

items.statement: If leptospiral contamination is considered possible or has occurred, promptly implement an appropriate corrective action plan in response to newly identified contamination sources, throughout the product life cycle.
items.quote: promptly implementing an appropriate corrective action plan in response to newly identified contamination sources, throughout the life cycle of the product
items.condition: if leptospiral contamination is considered possible or has occurred

items.statement: When assessing powder blend uniformity, evaluate all replicate samples taken from the various blender locations so that a statistically valid analysis is performed.
items.quote: The Agency currently recommends that all replicate samples taken from various locations in the blender be evaluated to perform a statistically valid analysis.

items.statement: Statistical tools may be used to determine both the number of replicates and the number of sampling locations across the blender to be analyzed for a valid analysis.
items.quote: Statistical tools are available to ascertain both the number of replicates and the number of sampling locations across the blender that should be analyzed to conduct a valid analysis.

items.statement: Do not extrapolate the results of the compendial uniformity of dosage units procedures to larger populations, because they are not a statistical sampling plan.
items.quote: However, the procedures and acceptance criteria in General Chapter <905> are not a statistical sampling plan and so the results of the procedures should not be extrapolated to larger populations.

items.statement: Make all sampling plans scientifically sound and representative of the batch under test.
items.quote: The CGMPs require that all sampling plans be scientifically sound and representative of the batch under test

items.statement: Perform in-process testing of powder blends to demonstrate adequacy of mixing.
items.quote: Further, in-process testing of powder blends to demonstrate adequacy of mixing is a CGMP requirement

items.statement: Evaluate between-location and within-location variability in the powder blend.
items.quote: Between- and within-location variability in the powder blend is a critical component of finished product quality and therefore should be evaluated.

items.statement: Use a science- and risk-based sampling approach to ensure (a) adequate blend mixing and (b) that the blend is sampled at a suitable point in the manufacturing process.
items.quote: Drug product manufacturers need to use a science- and risk-based sampling approach to ensure (a) adequacy of blend mixing and (b) that sampling of the blend is done at a suitable juncture in the manufacturing process.

items.statement: Design blend sampling and analysis to ensure there are no differences between locations in a blend that could adversely affect finished product quality.
items.quote: The sampling and analysis needs to ensure that no differences exist between locations in a blend that could adversely affect finished product quality.

items.statement: Adopt more innovative approaches to ensuring adequacy of powder blend mixing.
items.quote: The Agency encourages firms to adopt more innovative approaches to ensuring adequacy of mixing

items.statement: If a thief sampling method is proposed, evaluate its reliability as part of analytical methods development.
items.quote: If a manufacturer proposes to use a thief sampling method, the reliability of the method should be evaluated as part of analytical methods development.

not_applicable.text: Why is FDA concerned about proper sampling of powder blends?
Traditional sampling using a powder-thief may have drawbacks and limitations, such as causing disturbance
However, powder-thief sampling remains widely used and provides reliable results in many cases.

items.statement: Innovative approaches to ensuring adequate powder blend mixing may be considered, including but not limited to (a) PAT real-time monitoring and feed-forward control of the blending process and (b) statistical process control tools to monitor the blending process and maintain a state of control.
items.quote: Innovative approaches to consider include, but are not limited to: (a) PAT real-time monitoring and feed-forward controlling of the powder blending process (see the guidance for industry PAT—A Framework for Innovative Pharmaceutical Development, Manufacturing, and Quality Assurance) and (b) use of statistical process control tools to monitor the powder blending process and to maintain a state of control.

items.statement: When deciding to implement PAT or other process-monitoring and control techniques for assessing powder blend homogeneity, support the decision with appropriate data and rationale using a science- and risk-based approach.
items.quote: When a manufacturer decides to implement PAT or other process-monitoring and control techniques for powder blend homogeneity assessment, its decision should be supported with appropriate data and rationale using a science- and risk-based approach.
items.condition: when PAT or other monitoring techniques are used for blend homogeneity

items.statement: Estimate the effective sample size of powder examined by PAT probes so that the scale of scrutiny of PAT blend monitoring can be justified.
items.quote: For example, the effective sample size of powder examined by PAT probes has to be estimated such that the scale of scrutiny of the PAT powder blending monitoring can be justified

items.statement: Justify the number of PAT probes and their locations.
items.quote: The number of PAT probes and their locations also have to be justified.

items.quote: Stratified sampling is recommended to be used when the population is known to have several subdivisions (i.e., locations), which may give different results for the quality characteristics measured.
items.condition: population with subdivisions that may differ

items.quote: The Agency expects that no significant differences should exist between in-process locations that could affect finished product quality.

items.statement: Evaluate between-location and within-location variability of in-process dosage units.
items.quote: Between- and within-location variability is a critical component of finished product quality and therefore should be evaluated.

items.statement: For drug products not required to be sterile, establish and follow appropriate written procedures during manufacturing to prevent objectionable microorganisms.
items.quote: 21 CFR 211.113(a) requires appropriate written procedures to be established and followed during manufacturing to prevent objectionable microorganisms in drug products not required to be sterile.
items.condition: drug products not required to be sterile

items.statement: Do not use antimicrobial preservatives as a substitute for good manufacturing practices, solely to reduce the viable microbial population of a nonsterile product, or to control the presterilization bioburden of a multidose formulation during manufacturing.
items.quote: Antimicrobial preservatives should not be used as a substitute for good manufacturing practices, solely to reduce the viable microbial population of a nonsterile product, or control the presterilization bioburden of a multidose formulation during manufacturing.

items.statement: Do not rely on antimicrobial preservatives to bring initial out-of-specification plate counts down to within-specification levels and then market the product.
items.quote: Drug manufacturers should not rely on antimicrobial preservatives to reduce initial out-of-specification plate counts to within-specification levels and then market the product.

items.statement: Reject drug products that fail to meet established standards or specifications.
items.quote: Section 211.165(f) mandates that drug products failing to meet established standards or specifications be rejected.

items.statement: Reject the drug product on the basis of initial out-of-specification microbial results; these results are not disqualified even if later test results are within specification.
items.quote: The initial test results exhibiting out-of specification levels of microbes are not disqualified even if subsequent test results are within specifications. In such cases, FDA still expects the manufacturer to reject the drug product based on the initial results.

items.statement: Do not allow an inappropriately long time (for example weeks) to pass before testing the product, which could let the preservative reduce microbes introduced during manufacture and so avoid out-of-specification results.
items.quote: It is also not acceptable for manufacturers to allow an inappropriately long time (e.g., weeks) to pass before testing the product, which might permit the preservative to reduce levels of microbes possibly introduced during manufacture and thus avoid out-of-specification test results.

items.statement: Review the manufacturing process to identify procedures or equipment that might introduce contaminating microorganisms into the process or product.
items.quote: Finally, drug manufacturers should review their manufacturing process to determine procedures or equipment that might introduce contaminating microorganisms into the process or product.
